transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-06-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mike (Aurora Procurement), Sara (Aurora Legal), Rafael (Cloud Ops), Leah (Security), Tom (Finance)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for making time, um we'll run through objectives quick — procurement + legal sprint, align owners, and get the bench window scheduled. if you see anything missing shout up.

[00:18] Mike (Procurement): yeah thanks jordan, big calendar pinch for us this quarter so we want to get the MSA and DPA decisions done this sprint. scope is: pricing approvals, sla tiers, and KMS for keys. we also need to understand whether dedicated infra is a hard requirement from security.

[00:35] Jordan: totally, and just to frame — redwood supports hosted api, dedicated pools, and private vpc deployments. priya will jump into the technical constraints in a bit. from legal perspective, sara, do you have any top-of-mind non-starters?

[00:48] Sara (Legal): hi — thanks. nothing immediate non-starter but we're sensitive to two things: one, subprocessor list and right to audit; two, data retention / deletion guarantees esp for PHI-ish telemetry — aurora handles some regulated data. we need explicit KMS/customer-managed key language or an HSM option. also, the indemnity and liability caps — we'd like to propose a carveout for data breaches. i'll circulate redlines.

[01:10] Priya (SE): quick note — from infra side, dedicated pool gives you more predictable p99 latency and isolation for logs; hosted can be cheaper but shared noisy neighbors can spike tokens. we can demo cost deltas in the pricing worksheet.

[01:28] Leah (Security): if dedicated is the ask, we need to confirm network egress patterns and whether keys leave our VPC. our preference is bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with envelope encryption. does redwood support customer KMS via a private peering?

[01:45] Priya: yes, we can integrate with customer KMS via standard handshake; for private deployments we support either external KMS or hardware HSM depending on the package. there are a couple of implementation patterns — we can share tradeoffs in the tech doc.

[02:03] Tom (Finance): from our side, two big decision levers: committed reserved capacity vs on-demand hosted pricing and the time to realize discounts. we'll need SKU mapping to our internal chargeback model. also, are there early termination fees on reserved capacity?

[02:20] Jordan: good call. we'll include a reserved vs hosted comparison with break-even points. termination terms are negotiable depending on commitment length — i'll put options in the worksheet.

[02:33] (slight crosstalk) Rafael (Cloud Ops): one practical thing — our infra blocks egress to unknown IP ranges; we need a static set of egress IPs or a private link. what's the recommended connectivity?

[02:48] Priya: we support static egress ranges for our hosted offering and private link for dedicated/private deployments. we'll ask you to share the list of allowed ranges.

[03:02] Mike: timeline — procurement wants final commercial sign-off before our vendor committee review on 2026-06-21. so we need redlines and pricing by ~2026-06-12 to route internally.

[03:15] Jordan: understood — i'll aim for 2026-06-10 to send pricing and commercial terms. priya will book perf window. sara to provide legal redlines by the 12th.

[03:26] Sara: yes i'll try for the 12th, though i may need one follow-up question after i see the first pass.

[03:34] Priya: ok i'll go through the technical checklist now — for the perf test we'll want a representative prompt set, target p99 SLA goals, concurrency envelope, and token budgets. can aurora provide a synthetic corpus or do you want us to run with a sanitized sample?

[03:52] Rafael: we can sanitize a subset, but we need to ensure no PHI leaves our systems. if redwood can take sanitized test payloads via S3 presigned links and run in a dedicated pool under an NDA, that's okay.

[04:08] Priya: S3 presigned flow works; we'll run in isolated project namespace and ephemeral logs. note: some traces may still have token metadata — we'll describe retention.

[04:20] Leah: retention is critical — what is redwood's default token retention for hosted vs dedicated?

[04:28] Jordan: default hosted is 30 days for observability TTL, but we can offer shorter retention and opt-out for logs for dedicated + private plans. that's part of the pricing/contract conversation.

[04:42] (background noise) Mike: okay, two blockers for procurement: 1) DPA with subprocessor list and deletion proof; 2) pricing alignment for a three-month pilot with option to convert to reserved.

[04:55] Jordan: for pilots we often do a short reserved allocation with a conversion credit on full commit. i'll model that in the pricing worksheet.

[05:04] Tom: sounds good — also curious about credit terms and invoicing cadence. monthly invoicing with net-45 is what we typically do. any flexibility?

[05:13] Jordan: standard is net-30 for smaller customers, enterprise can ask for net-45; we'll flag that as negotiable.

[05:20] (pause) Priya: quick technical caveat — if you use heavy KV cache reuse patterns, the cost dynamics change. dedicated pool supports larger KV cache and persistent sessions which reduce cost per token for certain prompt patterns. we'll capture that in the technical appendix.

[05:40] Sara: on the DPA, specific ask: can redwood commit to annual subprocessor audits and provide a list with contactable subprocessor reps? we need transparency for our audits.

[05:54] Jordan: we can provide a subprocessor list and confirm SOC2 reports; annual audits for subprocessors are more complicated but we can provide attestations and contact points. we'll include SOC2/ISO artifacts in the packet.

[06:10] Rafael: one more network detail — egress charges. if we run a dedicated deployment in region X, are we billed for egress out of our cloud account or redwood handles that?

[06:23] Priya: typically egress is billed by customer cloud provider; for Redwood Dedicated we can offer an optional egress pass-through line item or allow customer to peer directly; we'll clarify in the worksheet.

[06:36] Mike: ok good.

[06:40] (silence) Jordan: will now do a rapid run of the proposed timeline and owners — 1) Jordan sends pricing + commercial options by 2026-06-10; 2) Priya books bench (week of 6/15) and shares test plan by 6/12; 3) Sara shares DPA redlines by 6/12; 4) Rafael provides VPC diagram and egress lists by 6/11; 5) Leah enumerates compliance artifacts needed by 6/14. any additions?

[07:05] Sara: maybe one add — we'll need to lock in a contact in Redwood for emergency incident handling and escalation path. can that be a named POC?

[07:12] Jordan: yes, we'll provide a named on-call contact and escalation matrix.

[07:18] Tom: finance wants to see an example invoice and billing schedule for the pilot path — can you attach a sample?

[07:25] Jordan: yes sample invoice and payment terms will be included.

[07:30] (crosstalk) Priya: one more note — for the perf bench if you want to simulate 95th and 99th percentile latencies we need to run at scaled concurrency, please identify expected user concurrency for peak traffic so we size the test.

[07:45] Rafael: peak is approx 120 concurrent sessions for the initial integration; could be spikey. we'll send a traffic profile.

[07:54] Mike: also we are evaluating competitor tech, anthropic and a proto in-house route, cost will matter but so will SLAs.

[08:02] Jordan: understood — i'll include a competitor comparison appendix focused on latency/cost for your use case.

[08:10] (short pause) Priya: need to capture one security nuance — if you require BYOK + private peering + dedicated pool there's an uplift for ops. we'll surface exact uplift in the pricing doc.

[08:25] Leah: ok.

[08:29] Jordan: great, wrap up then — recap of owners and deadlines, and i'll schedule a follow-up on 2026-06-14 to review pricing and legal redlines before your procurement committee. does that time work?

[08:44] Mike: 06-14 is fine. please also give us a short cheat-sheet we can use with internal stake holders.

[08:52] Jordan: will do — one-pager for execs + longer appendix for legal/infra.

[08:58] Sara: thanks everyone — expect redlines from me, and i'll flag anything that needs another legal call.

[09:06] Jordan: thanks all, we will follow up in the thread with links to SOC2, sample invoices, pricing worksheet, and the perf test plan.

[09:14] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription occasionally merged proper nouns; internal product names like "Redwood Dedicated" were sometimes transcribed as "red wood dedicated" or "red wood dedicated pool". timestamps are approximate.

Attachments / referenced artifacts: pricing-worksheet-draft.xlsx (to be shared), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, dpa-template-v1.docx, perf-test-plan-template.md, sample-invoice.pdf, vpc-connection-guide.zip

Recap / explicit next steps (verbatim):
- Jordan: Share updated pricing worksheet and sample invoice by 2026-06-10.
- Priya: Schedule performance benchmark week of 2026-06-15 and share test plan by 2026-06-12.
- Sara: Circulate DPA redlines and highlight retention / subprocessor concerns by 2026-06-12.
- Rafael: Provide VPC diagram, allowed egress IPs and traffic profile by 2026-06-11.
- Leah: Compile list of SOC2/ISO artifact requests and compliance checklist by 2026-06-14.

End of transcript.
